autumnwear.title: What to Wear in Japan in Late Autumn: 5 Tips
autumnwear.desc: Visiting Japan in late autumn? Bring layers: mornings and evenings can feel cool, while afternoons may be warmer. A light jacket or sweater is often enough in big cities. Wear comfy walking shoes, and slip-ons help where you need to remove shoes. Weather differs by region, and mountains can be much colder, so check the forecast. Get the free 1-page Japan Quick Start cheat sheet. #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan

eatwalk.title: Eating While Walking in Japan: 5 Tips for Visitors
eatwalk.desc: Is eating while walking OK in Japan? Many people eat food right where they bought it, and some streets and towns have signs asking you not to eat while walking. Bins can be hard to find, so carry a small bag for trash. Some convenience stores have a small eating space, while others don't. On busy streets, step aside before you eat or drink. Rules vary by area, so follow local signs. Get the free 1-page Japan Quick Start cheat sheet. #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan

Note: rules vary by area, follow local signs. Save this for your trip! Footer: free 1-page cheat sheet, Japan Quick Start.

help.title: When You Need Help in Japan: Numbers and Tips for Visitors
help.desc: Save these before your first trip to Japan: Call 110 for urgent police emergencies and 119 for urgent fire or medical emergencies. JNTO runs a 24/7 visitor hotline in English, Chinese and Korean; save the current details from the official JNTO website. Lost something? Ask station staff, the shop or your hotel first. More in JAPAN LIKE A LOCAL, a 13-page PDF guide for first-time visitors ($4.99). #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan
